newsitem.title: USA: Ziegler unit agrees to settle suit.
newsitem.headline: Ziegler unit agrees to settle suit.

text.p: B.C. Ziegler and Co, a broker-dealer subsidiary of Ziegler Cos Inc, said Friday it has reached a provisional settlement in a class action suit, which includes payment of $1.4 million.
Ziegler said it was made a party to a lawsuit involving the underwriting of two bond issues in May, 1989, which totaled $11,680,000.
Ziegler said the settlement amount will be taken as a charge against first quarter 1997 earnings.

Ziegler said the bonds were issued to construct a retirement facility. In 1992, there was a default on the bonds, which resulted in a significant loss of principal and interest by the bondholders, it added.
Ziegler said it admitted no liability with respect to the lawsuit in reaching a provisional settlement with attorneys representing a class of former bondholders.
The company said it agreed to the settlement to manage the uncertainty and expenses of protracted litigation.
The payment of $1.4 million is conditioned upon judicial approval.
